diagrams.title: Product Governance Loop
diagrams.summary: Odylith governs its own product backlog, plans, bugs, diagrams, and generated surfaces inside the public repo while consumers keep their own repo truth locally.
diagrams.read_guide: Start at Odylith product at the top, then move through Dashboard into the governed truth loop. Registry and Atlas explain what the components are; Radar and Technical Plans show how work is selected and planned; Compass and Casebook feed execution evidence and learning back into Radar.

components.name: casebook

diagrams.title: Context And Agent Execution Stack
diagrams.summary: Context and execution stack showing repo truth flowing through compiler-owned memory read models, the Context-to-Execution handshake, shared Execution Engine snapshot, visible intervention broker, and accuracy-first benchmark proof before routing, orchestration, or chatter act.
diagrams.read_guide: Start with CLI and repo truth entering Context Engine. Read the governed memory substrate as the evidence layer: bundle, snapshot, backend, remote retrieval, session stream, and contracts converge before decisions are made. Then follow the Context-to-Execution handshake into Execution Engine, and read outward to Delivery Intelligence, Tribunal, routing, orchestration, visible intervention, chatter, and benchmark proof.

components.name: Dossier builder
components.description: Delivery intelligence assembles one grounded case dossier with repo objects, checkpoints, approvals, and evidence before the actor pass starts.

components.name: Runtime truth and consumers

components.name: Queue rationale output

diagrams.title: Tribunal Adjudication, Editorial Merge, and Packet Assembly

components.name: Grounded dossier and actor pass
components.description: Tribunal builds one dossier and runs the full actor lattice over the same evidence before any editorial merge occurs.

components.name: Adjudication and provider validation
components.description: The adjudicator chooses the leading story and bounded provider refinements are accepted only when they validate against named evidence ids.

components.name: Editorial merge
components.description: Tribunal compresses the adjudicated outcome into a short queue headline and lead brief while keeping systemic and rival/risk context as separate outputs.

components.name: Packet assembly and feedback loop
components.description: Remediator compiles the bounded packet and Odylith later folds approval, delegation, apply, and clearance state back into posture.

diagrams.title: Subagent Router Decision and Escalation Flow
diagrams.summary: Decision flow for bounded subagent routing beneath the prompt-level orchestrator: intake, measured Odylith control-advisory assessment, graph-backed architecture-execution guards, confidence-backed profile selection, native spawn/close payload emission, rescope-vs-escalate outcomes, and family-aware adaptive tuning.

components.name: Route intake and assessment
components.description: The router normalizes bounded prompt metadata, scores ambiguity/risk/scope/validation signals, and assigns task family plus route confidence before delegation.

components.name: Measured control-advisory layer
components.description: The router now reads one bounded Odylith advisory contract compiled from the local evaluation ledger, carrying measured state/confidence plus depth/delegation/parallelism/budget/retrieval/speed posture, and also respects architecture-dossier execution hints when topology grounding is weak or high-risk.

components.name: Profile selection, confidence backstop, and xhigh gate
components.description: Weighted profile scoring chooses among Spark and GPT-5.4 tiers, low-confidence writes can be promoted to stronger GPT-5.4 profiles, grounded high-risk architecture slices can earn the strongest bounded lane, and `xhigh` remains separately gated by critical risk or maximum-accuracy feature conditions.

components.name: Validation, rescope, and adaptive loop
components.description: One spawned subagent is validated explicitly, may escalate once, may instead return control to the main thread for local rescope, and now emits native spawn-agent plus closeout payloads that keep the host thread aligned with the routed contract.

diagrams.title: Subagent Router Governance and Audit Topology
diagrams.summary: Governance topology for the Subagent Router as the bounded leaf-routing layer beneath the Subagent Orchestrator, including thin skills, route-confidence outputs, native spawn/close payloads, the local evaluation-to-advisory control loop, Compass audit stream, Registry manifest, living spec, runbook, and Atlas coverage.

components.name: Operator and execution surface
components.description: The main agent or maintainer invokes the thin skill and router script, which choose one worker profile for bounded delegation and emit route-confidence plus native host-call payloads.

components.name: Local state and forensic audit
components.description: Local evaluation and tuning state plus optional Compass timeline events preserve explainability, measured control advisories, family-aware adaptation, and feedback without creating tracked runtime truth.

components.name: Registry and Atlas governance
components.description: The component manifest, living spec, runbook, and diagram metadata make the routing policy inspectable across Registry, Atlas, Compass, and the tooling shell as a governed AI execution surface.

diagrams.title: Subagent Orchestrator Prompt Triage and Routing Flow
diagrams.summary: Prompt-level orchestration flow from an evidence-grounded repo-work prompt across the consumer lane, pinned dogfood, and detached `source-local` maintainer-dev posture through measured Odylith control advisories, architecture-dossier execution hints, local-only gates, orchestration-mode selection, and per-leaf handoff into the bounded Subagent Router, including native spawn and closeout payloads for host execution.

components.name: Evidence grounding and request shaping
components.description: The main thread grounds the evidence cone first, then converts the substantive grounded repo-work prompt into an orchestration request with candidate paths, acceptance criteria, validation commands, and accuracy posture.

components.name: Prompt triage and orchestration mode selection
components.description: The orchestrator evaluates hard local-only gates, measured control advisories, architecture execution hints, and conservative parallel-safety rules to choose `local_only`, `single_leaf`, `serial_batch`, or `parallel_batch`.

components.name: Leaf-routing handoff
components.description: Every delegated leaf is routed through Subagent Router for explicit model plus reasoning selection, while the orchestrator keeps merge ownership and now carries native spawn-agent plus closeout payloads, compact control-advisory posture, and architecture risk/fanout hints in the main-thread execution plan.

diagrams.title: Subagent Orchestrator Safe Fan-Out and Parallel Safety
diagrams.summary: Parallel-safety decision tree for automatic orchestration, including read-only fan-out caps, disjoint-write checks, coupled-path downgrades, native per-leaf spawn/close payloads, and the local fallback path when any leaf becomes unsafe.

components.name: Safety classification
components.description: The orchestrator classifies grounded prompts into `read_only_safe`, `disjoint_write_safe`, `serial_ordered`, or `local_only` based on path ownership, criticality, and validation clarity.

components.name: Conservative batch shaping
components.description: Read-only work may split into a small parallel batch, disjoint writes may split into a smaller capped batch, and coupled docs/tests/skills/contracts/tooling work is downgraded to serial or local execution.

components.name: Leaf fallback and safety override
components.description: Even after prompt-level decomposition, any leaf-router `main_thread` refusal collapses the whole orchestration plan back to local rescope instead of forcing unsafe fan-out, and accepted leaves still carry native spawn/close payloads for the main thread.

diagrams.title: Subagent Orchestrator Merge Barrier and Adjudication Ownership
diagrams.summary: Main-thread ownership model for serial and parallel orchestration, covering dependency barriers, cross-leaf merge responsibility, local rescope fallbacks, native closeout payload application, and the rule that architectural adjudication never belongs to a worker leaf.

components.name: Serial dependency ownership
components.description: Ordered leaves expose explicit dependency ids so the main thread controls when the next leaf may start and whether earlier results require local correction first.

components.name: Parallel merge barrier
components.description: Parallel leaves run only on disjoint owned paths, but the main thread still owns merge, final validation, cross-leaf acceptance, and delegated-leaf closeout before any result is treated as landed.

components.name: Rescope and adjudication fallback
components.description: If a leaf route or escalation reveals broader coordination, design conflict, or unclear ownership, control returns to the main thread rather than bouncing the ambiguity between workers.

diagrams.title: Subagent Orchestrator Governance and Adaptive Learning Topology

components.name: Policy and operator surface

components.name: Local adaptive state and audit

components.name: Registry and Atlas governance

diagrams.title: Anti-Slop Governance And Host Parity
diagrams.summary: Shows how anti-slop guidance, skills, install-generated mirrors, Codex and Claude host surfaces, hygiene enforcement, benchmark acceptance, and browser proof stay aligned so structural cleanup does not drift behavior or cross-host contracts.
diagrams.read_guide: Read the two top boxes as the governing promise and the workstream program that delivers it. Then read the grouped containers: canonical truth defines the rules, generated parity keeps host mirrors aligned, host execution surfaces show where Codex and Claude consume the rules, and runtime cleanup plus release proof shows how structural work is validated before it can be claimed.

diagram_boxes.label: Anti-slop contract
diagram_boxes.description: This is the rule the whole diagram protects: no temporary shim ownership, no fake cleanup, and no broad structural claim without behavior proof and structural proof.

diagram_boxes.label: B-110 umbrella
diagram_boxes.description: This ties the anti-slop work to the B-110 discipline program, including host parity work and release-proof surfaces.

diagram_boxes.label: Canonical product truth
diagram_boxes.description: This group holds the source-of-truth rules and plans. The boxes inside it define what agents and host surfaces must follow.

diagram_boxes.label: AGENTS + host contracts
diagram_boxes.description: These files carry the instructions that Codex, Claude, and installed host surfaces read before they act.

diagram_boxes.label: ANTI_SLOP_AND_DECOMPOSITION
diagram_boxes.description: This is the portable anti-slop policy. It explains what counts as real ownership movement, real decomposition, and acceptable proof.

diagram_boxes.label: odylith-code-hygiene-guard
diagram_boxes.description: This skill turns the anti-slop policy into an agent workflow for cleanup, review, and validation pressure.

diagram_boxes.label: B-110 technical plan
diagram_boxes.description: This plan breaks the discipline and anti-slop work into waves and names the validation evidence each wave must produce.

diagram_boxes.label: Generated parity and owned mirrors
diagram_boxes.description: Canonical guidance is copied into generated assets and mirrored host files while the checked-in source remains the single source of truth.

diagram_boxes.label: Atlas catalog + Mermaid source
diagram_boxes.description: Atlas stores this topology and gives the repo a governed diagram record that can be refreshed and reviewed.

diagram_boxes.label: Compass timeline evidence
diagram_boxes.description: Compass records execution evidence so cleanup and host-parity claims have a timeline, not just a final statement.

diagram_boxes.label: Install generators
diagram_boxes.description: The install generators produce managed host guidance and bootstrap assets from Odylith-owned source.

diagram_boxes.label: Bundled mirrors
diagram_boxes.description: These are the shipped copies of host guidance, such as project-root `.claude` assets. They must match the canonical rules.

diagram_boxes.label: Governed refresh lanes
diagram_boxes.description: Atlas refresh and Odylith sync regenerate governed surfaces after source truth changes, keeping diagrams, dashboards, and payloads aligned.

diagram_boxes.label: Cross-host execution surfaces
diagram_boxes.description: This group shows where the same anti-slop contract is consumed by Codex, Claude, and CLI shortcut flows.

diagram_boxes.label: Codex surface
diagram_boxes.description: Codex reads repo AGENTS guidance and the shared runtime contract, so its cleanup behavior follows the same rules as other hosts.

diagram_boxes.label: Claude surface
diagram_boxes.description: Claude reads the managed `.claude` guidance, reviewer routing, and skill set, so it stays aligned with the same anti-slop policy.

diagram_boxes.label: CLI fast paths
diagram_boxes.description: The simple `Odylith, help` and `show me what you can do` paths must stay clear and must not be intercepted by heavyweight guidance.

diagram_boxes.label: Runtime cleanup and release proof
diagram_boxes.description: This group shows the proof path for structural cleanup: inventory, ownership movement, validation, browser proof, benchmark acceptance, and release accountability.

diagram_boxes.label: Structural inventory
diagram_boxes.description: This records the current cleanup pressure, such as red-zone file counts and helper drift, before claiming structural improvement.

diagram_boxes.label: Ownership moves
diagram_boxes.description: This is where real ownership is moved into the right modules and support owners instead of leaving shim walls behind.

diagram_boxes.label: Hygiene enforcement
diagram_boxes.description: This checks that cleanup did not create new helper drift, shim boundaries, or vague shared ownership.

diagram_boxes.label: Discipline + guidance-behavior validators
diagram_boxes.description: These validators prove that guidance and discipline behavior still work after structural changes.

diagram_boxes.label: Benchmark acceptance
diagram_boxes.description: Benchmark acceptance blocks public claims until the relevant benchmark family and publication guard pass.

diagram_boxes.label: Headless browser proof
diagram_boxes.description: Browser proof checks rendered Atlas, Compass, and shell states so surface claims are validated in the UI, not only in source files.

diagram_boxes.label: Release-proof accountability
diagram_boxes.description: This is the closeout checkpoint: behavior must keep working while the structure improves, and the release evidence has to show both.

diagrams.title: Migration Runtime Upgrade Transaction Flow
diagrams.summary: Shows how install, upgrade, reinstall, doctor, and release gates flow through the migration runtime before mutation.
diagrams.read_guide: Read the center column from top to bottom first. It shows how Odylith turns a command into one shared migration plan. Then read the branches from MigrationPlan: dry-run previews the plan, upgrade applies it, doctor explains current health, the release gate checks release readiness, and any unsafe state stops before runtime files change.

diagram_boxes.label: Operator command
diagram_boxes.description: The operator runs install, upgrade, reinstall, doctor, or release migration-gate. All of them enter the same planner, so the answer does not depend on which command asked.

diagram_boxes.label: Resolve target release
diagram_boxes.description: Odylith identifies the release being installed or checked, then gathers the release manifest, schema, and required verification evidence.

diagram_boxes.label: Repo scenario classifier
diagram_boxes.description: Odylith inspects the repository and names the situation: installed, legacy, source-local, stale ledger, missing launcher, or another known state.

diagram_boxes.label: Migration registry
diagram_boxes.description: Odylith looks up the migrations that are allowed for this release. Each registered migration says when it applies, what it may write, and how it is verified.

diagram_boxes.label: MigrationPlan
diagram_boxes.description: This is the single plan every command uses. It says which migrations will run, which are already satisfied, which are skipped, and which are blocked.

diagram_boxes.label: Dry-run and JSON report
diagram_boxes.description: Dry-run shows the scenario, planned file writes, rollback scope, selected migrations, blockers, and plan fingerprint without changing the repo.

diagram_boxes.label: Upgrade/apply execution
diagram_boxes.description: Upgrade applies only the migrations selected by the shared plan. It does not make a second private decision about what should run.

diagram_boxes.label: Durable migration ledger
diagram_boxes.description: After apply, Odylith records what it checked, what it planned to write, what it actually wrote, and which verification passed.

diagram_boxes.label: Doctor observability
diagram_boxes.description: Doctor explains whether migrations are pending, blocked, stale, or only need repair cleanup. It reports health without silently applying release migrations.

diagram_boxes.label: Release migration gate
diagram_boxes.description: Before release, this gate proves that required migrations are registered, tested with fixtures, and not bypassed by install or upgrade paths.

diagram_boxes.label: Fail closed before runtime mutation
diagram_boxes.description: If proof is missing or the ledger is stale, Odylith stops before changing runtime files. Unsafe migration states fail closed.

diagram_boxes.label: Post-upgrade surfaces
diagram_boxes.description: Dashboards and generated pages refresh after migration work. They are kept separate so a rendering refresh is not mistaken for a migration.
